Candidate 1 (C383): NON-ABELIAN RECIPROCITY ON UNIVERSAL MODULI STACKS AND AUTOMORPHIC REPRESENTATIONS
Claim 1: Automorphic representations on higher-rank unitary groups associated to universal moduli stacks over P^1 \ {0, 1, inf} eliminate Beal solutions across varying triple exponents (p, q, r).
Method 1: Non-abelian class field theory, automorphic Galois representations, and Arthur-Clozel-Fontaine-Mazur compatibility.

Candidate 2 (C384): RELATIVE DERIVED MODULI OF LOCAL SYSTEMS AND CHARACTER VARIETIES OVER SPEC Z
Claim 2: Relative derived character varieties RMap(pi_1(P^1 \ {0, 1, inf}), GL_n) over Spec Z impose non-trivial obstruction classes forbidding Beal solutions.
Method 2: Relative derived algebraic geometry, representation varieties, and schematization of homotopy types.

compatible.instructions: Are these two candidates mathematically compatible, operating on complementary aspects of the conjecture?

criteria.true: Yes, one provides input to the other or they address complementary signatures/invariants.
criteria.false: No, they operate in disjoint or contradictory frameworks.

combination_value.instructions: What value would combining these two candidate approaches create?
criteria: level 0: Zero value; combination fails or is identical to one candidate alone.
level 1: Minor bookkeeping convenience without resolving open obstacles.
level 2: Discharges a specific open obligation in one of the candidates.
level 3: Opens a genuine new attack route avoiding known dead ends.

shared_failure.instructions: Do both candidates fail due to the same fundamental obstruction (e.g. deformation invariance, Selmer blowup, or heuristic laundering)?

criteria.true: Yes, both share the same failure mode and combining them provides no new leverage.
criteria.false: No, they hit independent failure modes, offering structural contrast.
